Surface temperature referred to an elevation datum

Source: R/metric-dt.R
ef_ts_datum.Rd

Adjusts the land surface temperature to a common elevation datum with a constant lapse rate of the surface temperature with elevation, so that the near-surface temperature difference \(dT\) of METRIC is calibrated and applied on temperatures that are comparable across elevations. The datum temperature is used only for \(dT\); air density, pressure, roughness and wind use the actual elevation.

Usage

ef_ts_datum(lst, elevation, datum_elevation, lapse_rate)

Arguments

lst

Numeric. Land surface temperature \(T_s\) [K]. Must be finite and > 0.

elevation

Numeric. Elevation of the pixel \(z\) [m]. Must be finite.

datum_elevation

Numeric scalar. Elevation of the datum \(z_{datum}\) [m]. Must be finite. A constant of the scene, recorded with the calibration: it changes the reported intercept a, not the sensible heat flux (see Details).

lapse_rate

Numeric scalar. Lapse rate of the surface temperature with elevation \(\Gamma\) [K m-1] (note: per metre, not per kilometre). Must be finite and >= 0. No default (decision SH-13): the SEBAL Idaho manual uses 0.0065 K m-1 (Waters et al., 2002, Eq. 12-7), the water package 0.00649 K m-1, and METRIC tailors the lapse rate to the scene, with separate rates for flat and mountainous terrain (Allen et al., 2012, p. 74).

Value

A numeric vector of datum temperature \(T_{s,datum}\) [K], with the common length of lst and elevation and keeping their dim.

Details

$$T_{s,datum} = T_s + \Gamma\,(z - z_{datum})$$

The value of \(z_{datum}\) does not affect the calibrated \(dT\) nor the sensible heat flux (author's derivation, dev/specs/sensible-heat.md section 9.1): shifting the datum shifts every datum temperature by the same amount, which the two-anchor linear relation absorbs in its intercept. Only \(\Gamma\) matters.

Missing values propagate. Infinite values and values outside the domain raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error).

Verification status: the form is VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): Waters et al. (2002), appendix 12, p. 96, Eq. 12-7 (\(T_{s,dem} = T_s + 0.0065\,\Delta z\), with \(\Delta z\) the elevation of the pixel minus that of the datum, usually the weather station). The "dual-stage" correction of METRIC for mountains (Allen et al., 2012, p. 74) is not implemented. The cross-check with Allen et al. (2007) remains desirable but is no longer blocking.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

Allen, R. G., Kjaersgaard, J. H., Trezza, R., Oliveira, A., Robison, C., & Lorite-Torres, I. (2012). Refining components of a satellite-based surface energy balance model to complex land-use systems. In Remote Sensing and Hydrology (IAHS Publication 352, pp. 73-75). IAHS Press.

See also

Other aerodynamics and sensible heat functions: ef_air_density(), ef_blending_wind(), ef_calibrate_h(), ef_dt_coef(), ef_h_control(), ef_rah(), ef_sensible_heat(), ef_ustar(), ef_zom()

Examples

# Pixels at 500 m and 700 m referred to a 500 m datum
ef_ts_datum(lst = c(300, 316), elevation = c(500, 700),
            datum_elevation = 500, lapse_rate = 0.00649)
#> [1] 300.000 317.298
